title: RAD 111 - Introduction to Radiography: X-Rays, Equipment and Imaging

items.q: Absorbed dose may be defined as
o: unwanted general blackening of the film that does not belong to the image
the amount of radiation energy taken up per unit mass of tissue
the solution that removes undeveloped silver and hardens the emulsion
natural radiation present in the environment from soil, space and building materials
items.s: Absorbed dose: the amount of radiation energy taken up per unit mass of tissue. The other options describe Film fog, Fixer, Background radiation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Absorbed dose?
o: the amount of radiation energy taken up per unit mass of tissue
the adjustable device that limits the beam to the area of interest
a penetrating form of electromagnetic radiation produced inside an X-ray tube

items.s: Absorbed dose: the amount of radiation energy taken up per unit mass of tissue. The other options describe Collimator, Penetration, X-ray.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Radiography.
o: the coiled wire that emits electrons when it is heated

the branch of medicine concerned with producing and interpreting medical images
the range of duties a radiographer is trained and permitted to perform
items.s: Radiography: the imaging discipline that uses X-rays to show the inside of the body. The other options describe Scope of practice, Radiology, Filament.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Control panel.
o: the degree of blackening of the film after processing
a plate of thin lead strips that removes scattered radiation before the detector

the protective garment worn by staff who remain near an exposure
items.s: Control panel: the console where the radiographer sets and fires the exposure. The other options describe Anti-scatter grid, Lead apron, Film density.

items.q: The statement “the ability of X-rays to pass through solid matter” describes which of the following?

Differential absorption

Scatter radiation
items.s: Penetration is the ability of X-rays to pass through solid matter.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Optimisation?

items.s: Optimisation: the process of obtaining adequate image quality at the lowest practical exposure. The other options describe Equivalent dose, Personal monitoring, Background radiation.

the light-tight room where film is unloaded, processed and dried
the degree of blackening of the film after processing
unwanted general blackening of the film that does not belong to the image
items.s: Film emulsion: the light-sensitive coating of silver halide on the film base. The other options describe Film density, Film fog, Darkroom.

items.s: Radiograph: the visible image recorded when X-rays pass through a part of the body. The other options describe Diagnostic imaging, Scope of practice, Radiographer.

items.s: Latent image: the invisible change in the emulsion before chemical development begins. The other options describe Darkroom, Developer, Film fog.
